# HarnessDeck v0.1.0

The first release under your own brand and repository. HarnessDeck is the renamed
fork of DSH Studio: a native Tauri 2 desktop shell that supervises the DeepSeek
Harness on loopback, reclaims every process it spawns, and stays out of the way
of the harness UI. This cut also resolves two inherited supply-chain advisories.

## Added

- **Multi-project workspaces.** The window hosts a roster of on-disk projects,
  each bound to its own DSH Profile, with per-project session memory and
  isolated credentials. Switching projects restarts the supervised Harness into
  the right workspace.
- **Brand takeover.** The product, deep-link protocol (`harnessdeck://`),
  identifier (`app.harnessdeck`) and metadata are yours. The managed runtime
  integration is now `@duyanta123/harnessdeck-integration`, the plugin SDK is
  `@duyanta123/harnessdeck-sdk`, and the launcher injects `HARNESSDECK_*`
  environment values.
- **Signing and packaging.** The updater is armed with the fork's own minisign
  key (`createUpdaterArtifacts` on), release jobs target this repository, and
  the channel manifests regenerate as `harnessdeck` artifacts.

## Secured

- Pinned the managed runtime's package manager to pnpm 11.8.0, closing the
  configDependencies path-traversal advisory (CVE-2026-59195) that affected
  11.7.0 in the shipping runtime tree.
- The inherited glib 0.18 dependency carries a moderate
  `VariantStrIter` unsoundness advisory from the gtk-rs tree Tauri pins; it is
  not exercised by this application and is expected to resolve with the next
  Tauri update.

## Install and update

Existing `~/.dsh` Profiles, plugins, workspaces, sessions and credentials are
preserved. Verify downloads with `SHA256SUMS.txt`; in-app updates require the
Tauri updater signature. Windows, Linux and macOS assets are built from the same
release tag; no physical Apple device is available, so macOS flows are
compile-and-headless-boot verified but not physical-device validated.
